reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2, E3) from a single study on a VZrHfNbTa HEA substrate supports the formation of an HfZr interdiffusion layer, a ~120 μm coating, and a dense HfO2 scale that reduces oxidation. However, the hypothesis applies these findings to a different substrate (Zr-alloy cladding) without citing evidence that the same interdiffusion and protective behavior occurs on conventional Zr alloys, which is a key gap.
premises: Hot-press sintering of a hafnium coating on a Zr-containing substrate forms an interdiffused HfZr transition layer
The Hf coating thickness of ~120 μm is achievable and yields a diffusion distance of ~60 μm for Zr
Upon high-temperature oxidation, the Hf-coated composite forms a dense HfO2 protective layer
The HfO2 scale significantly reduces oxidation weight gain compared to uncoated material
The cited evidence on VZrHfNbTa HEA substrate is directly transferable to Zr-alloy cladding
